tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis:
- The recorded session shows a full flow: navigate to Magento admin orders URL (which redirects to login when unauthenticated), log in using visible username/password fields, land on the Orders grid at /admin/sales_order/index/, apply a filter on the "Order #" column, use the Search button to narrow results, verify the "Export to" dropdown and Export button, and finally click Export to trigger a CSV download of the filtered grid.
- It also demonstrates that the previous failing selector for the username input (input[name="login[username]"][type="text"]) is not reliable. Instead, the agent successfully used generic visible inputs indexed by position with associated element_hashes on the login form and on the grid.

2) Task Definition:
- Purpose of the tool: starting from anywhere (we will directly hit the orders URL), authenticate into Magento admin using known credentials, navigate to the Sales > Orders grid, optionally apply an order-number filter, choose an export format (CSV or Excel XML) from the export dropdown, and click the Export button so Magento generates and returns a file representing the current grid (filtered set) in machine-readable format.

3) Action Plan (Tool Steps):
- Step A: navigation → Go directly to http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/sales_order/ (starting URL). Magento will redirect to login if not authenticated.
- Step B: agentic step to log in → Because previous strict CSS selector for username failed and the demo successfully used generic inputs for username/password, we should let an agentic step handle locating the "User Name" and "Password" fields plus the Login button using visible labels rather than brittle selectors. This robustly addresses the prior failure.
- Step C: navigation → Go directly to /index.php/admin/sales_order/index/ to ensure we are on the main Orders grid (Magento often redirects there after login, but explicit navigation is deterministic).
- Step D: (optional filtering based on parameters) → If an order number filter value is provided, type it into the Order # filter input (using the demonstrated element with element_hash 230585ef85) and click the Search button (element_hash 97fc049eac). To keep the tool sequential and simple, we will perform these interactions whenever filter_order_increment_id is non-empty; the runtime that binds inputs can decide to pass empty when no filtering is desired.
- Step E: select export format in the Export-to dropdown at the top right of the grid. This is the select element with element_hash 0e5d7d55cb (and name sales_order_grid_export) and has options "CSV" and "Excel XML" as demonstrated. We will change its value based on the requested export_format parameter.
- Step F: click the Export button immediately to the right of the dropdown. In the final stable view, this is the button with element_hash e7272b642e (highlight index 126) whose label is "Export". Clicking it triggers download of the grid in the chosen format.

4) Variable Identification:
- login_username (string, required): value for the admin username; from the session this was "admin".
- login_password (string, required): value for the admin password; from the session this was "password123".
- filter_order_increment_id (string, optional): text to put into the "Order #" filter box (e.g., "000000299"). If empty, the Search step will still execute but effectively retain the default unfiltered grid.
- export_format (string, required, enum ["CSV", "Excel XML"]): which option to select in the Export dropdown. Session used "CSV", but the page also supports "Excel XML".

We do NOT introduce unnecessary inputs such as date ranges or other filters, because the core task is exporting the current (optionally filtered) grid and the recording only demonstrated order-number filtering. Those could be added in another tool.

5) Step Optimization:
- Navigation: Instead of separate Sales menu clicks, it is sufficient and more deterministic to go directly to /admin/sales_order/ and then /admin/sales_order/index/ via navigation actions, as demonstrated by the session URLs.
- Login selectors: the previous failure log shows a brittle CSS selector that no longer matches. The demo uses index-based interactions with element_hash to target username, password, and login. To fully decouple from index instability and timing, we wrap login in a single agent step that uses visible labels; this directly addresses the prior failure cause (missing selector / timing) while still being reliable.
- Orders grid interactions: once on /admin/sales_order/index/, the tool can use deterministic interactions with the known hash-marked elements: input 230585ef85 for the Order # filter, button 97fc049eac for Search, select 0e5d7d55cb for export format, and button  e7272b642e for Export.
- URL manipulation optimization: Magento’s grid filtering is done via POST and form submission (not simple GET query parameters), and export is triggered by a form submit as well, so replacing with crafted URLs is not appropriate. Keeping direct UI interactions is correct here.

Overall, the tool will:
1) Navigate → orders URL (which shows login if needed).
2) Agent → log in with provided credentials via visible username/password fields and Login button (avoids brittle selector).
3) Navigate → direct Orders grid URL.
4) Input → optional Order # filter and click Search.
5) SelectChange → choose export format.
6) Click → Export button to download file.

Because the main previous failure was on the login selector, the critical fix is using an agentic login step rather than a strict CSS selector; for grid export controls we can safely use deterministic element_hash-based selectors demonstrated in the session.
name: tool_export_orders_v5
description: Log into Magento admin, optionally filter the Sales > Orders grid, choose an export format, and click Export to download the current (optionally filtered) orders grid in machine-readable format (CSV or Excel XML). This version avoids brittle login selectors and uses stable interactions for the orders export controls.

steps.description: Go directly to the Magento admin Sales Orders URL, which will redirect to login if the session is not authenticated.

Log in to the Magento Admin Panel by filling the 'User Name' and 'Password' fields and submitting the login form, using the provided credentials. This avoids brittle CSS selectors that previously failed.
steps.task: On the current page, log into the Magento Admin Panel using username '{login_username}' and password '{login_password}'. Locate the 'User Name' text input, type the username, locate the 'Password' input, type the password, and submit the form via the Login button. Wait until the admin dashboard or an admin section loads successfully.

steps.description: Ensure we are on the main Orders grid page after login by navigating directly to the index view for Sales > Orders.
If an order-number filter is provided, type it into the 'Order #' filter field in the Orders grid header row. If the string is empty, this will simply leave the field blank.
Click the 'Search' button in the Orders grid controls to apply the current filter values (including any Order # filter).
Select the desired export format (CSV or Excel XML) in the 'Export to:' dropdown above the Orders grid using the export_format parameter.
Click the 'Export' button next to the 'Export to:' dropdown to trigger export of the current (optionally filtered) orders grid in the chosen format.

input_schema.name: login_username
input_schema.description: Magento admin username to authenticate with (e.g. 'admin').

input_schema.name: login_password
input_schema.description: Magento admin password to authenticate with (e.g. 'password123').

input_schema.name: filter_order_increment_id
input_schema.description: Optional order increment ID to filter by in the Orders grid 'Order #' filter field (e.g. '000000299'). Leave empty to export all visible orders without additional order-number filtering.

input_schema.name: export_format
input_schema.description: Desired export format from the 'Export to:' dropdown. Must match one of the visible options: 'CSV' or 'Excel XML'.
